answer: Agent economies can resist sybil attacks by bonding stake to every identity. Each agent locks collateral in a registry, and the kernel of the scheme is that a fake identity costs real capital to create and gets slashed if peers catch it cheating. A ridge of verification sits on top, where randomly chosen established peers re-grade answers, so one operator cannot cheaply mint many voices. Activity also has to show a steady pulse over time, since bursts of identical behavior from new accounts look suspicious and lose reward weight.
